questions.question: Which river is commonly called the Yellow River?
choices: Mekong
Ganges
Huang He
Yangtze

questions.question: Which dynasty is associated with oracle-bone inscriptions?
choices: Shang
Ming
Qing
Yuan

questions.question: What was the Mandate of Heaven?
choices: A rule requiring every ruler to be elected
A promise that dynasties could never fall
A contract ending warfare among all kingdoms
A belief that a ruler's authority depended on heavenly approval

questions.question: Which thinker emphasized ethical conduct, family relationships, and responsible leadership?
choices: Laozi
Confucius
Siddhartha Gautama
Socrates

questions.question: Which dynasty first unified China into an empire in 221 BCE?
choices: Qin
Han
Tang
Song

questions.question: Which philosophy emphasized strict laws and strong state authority?
choices: Buddhism
Daoism
Legalism
Confucianism

questions.question: What were the Silk Roads?
choices: One paved road built by a single emperor
Defensive walls around every Chinese city
Canals used only for moving soldiers
Networks of trade routes connecting regions across Eurasia

questions.question: How did river valleys support early Chinese settlement?
choices: They removed the risk of destructive floods
They provided water and fertile soil for farming
They prevented exchange between neighboring communities
They supplied the same crops in every climatic zone

questions.question: How could the Mandate of Heaven be used to justify replacing a dynasty?
choices: A failing ruler could be described as having lost heavenly approval
A dynasty automatically ended after one year
A ruler's ancestry was considered irrelevant to all politics
A foreign merchant could select any new emperor

questions.question: Why did Qin rulers standardize weights, measures, and writing?
choices: To give each region complete political independence
To end taxation throughout the empire
To make administration and exchange more consistent
To eliminate the use of written records

questions.question: What does filial piety mean in Confucian thought?
choices: Avoiding duties to family members
Choosing officials through hereditary military rank
Treating commercial profit as the highest moral goal
Respecting and fulfilling responsibilities toward parents and elders

questions.question: How does Daoism differ from an approach that emphasizes detailed coercive laws?
choices: It makes conquest the central goal of every ruler
It emphasizes living in harmony with the Dao and natural patterns
It requires all households to join the same bureaucracy
It treats punishment as the sole route to social order

questions.question: Why did Han governments need educated officials?
choices: A large empire required records, administration, and policy enforcement
The emperor personally handled every village dispute
Written government records had been outlawed
Merchants had replaced all regional government offices

questions.question: How did Silk Road commerce affect culture as well as trade?
choices: It prevented religions from crossing borders
It eliminated regional differences in language
It carried ideas, technologies, and beliefs between societies
It required all traders to live permanently in China

questions.question: Why did some Chinese rulers build or connect northern defensive walls?
choices: To irrigate every southern rice field
To block all contact with coastal markets
To create canals between the Yellow and Yangtze rivers
To help defend frontier areas against raids and invasion

questions.question: Which sequence correctly orders these Chinese dynasties?
choices: Han → Qin → Zhou → Shang
Shang → Zhou → Qin → Han
Zhou → Han → Shang → Qin
Qin → Shang → Han → Zhou

questions.question: An oracle bone records a ruler's question about a coming harvest. What does it most directly reveal?
choices: The connection between royal decision-making and divination
The use of elected assemblies to set agricultural policy
The absence of concern about farming in royal government
The practice of recording only completed events, not questions

questions.question: A teacher says that the Great Wall was built in one project by one ancient ruler. Which correction is most accurate?
choices: The wall was built entirely during the Shang dynasty
The walls were constructed mainly as irrigation channels
Different states and dynasties built and rebuilt walls over time
All surviving walls date to the Qin unification project

questions.question: Which policy would most closely reflect Confucian ideals of government?
choices: Ignoring education when appointing public officials
Replacing family responsibilities with military service
Encouraging rulers to rely only on secret punishments
Expecting leaders to set a moral example for others

questions.question: Roman glass found at a Chinese site would most reasonably support which conclusion?
choices: Rome directly supervised commercial policy in Chinese cities
Goods could travel long distances through connected trade networks
Roman merchants were the only traders permitted in China
Chinese communities relied entirely on imported glass production
